# Mahāmaṅgalajātaka (Ja 453)

**ID:** Ja 453
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Mahāmaṅgalajātaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul9.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahāmaṅgalajātaka* (Ja 453) is a Jātaka tale set at Jetavana, framed by the Buddha in connection with the *Mahāmaṅgala-sutta* (or the Treatise on Omens), opening with the prompt "Declare the truth". The verses in the text address the nature of auspicious signs (*maṅgala*) and faith. David J. Kalupahana observes that the teaching on practical blessings elucidated in the *Mahāmangala-sutta* and the *Svastyāyana-gāthā* also occurs in the *Mahāmaṅgala-jātaka*, testifying to the antiquity of these traditional blessings [Kalupahana 2001]. Discussing early conceptions of faith (*saddhā*) in canonical Pali literature, B. C. Law notes that the *Mahāmaṅgalajātaka* contains a verse reflecting early Indian notions of religious gift-giving, asserting that food, drink, garlands, perfumes, and unguents offered by the faithful with a contented mind serve as causes of celestial rebirth [Law 1931].

Regarding parallels and textual transmission, B. M. Barua identified chapter 38 of the Chinese *Fa-kheu-king* as a translation of an Indian recension of the *Mahāmaṅgalajātaka* [Barua 1921].

**Sources**

- [Kalupahana 2001] David J. Kalupahana, Buddhist Thought and Ritual (2001) — Discussed the antiquity of the blessings shared between the sutta, the Svastyāyana-gāthā, and the Jātaka.
- [Law 1931] Bimala Churn Law (ed.), Buddhistic Studies (1931) — Quoted and analyzed a verse from the Jātaka regarding faith and offerings.
- [Barua 1921] Benimadhab Barua, Prakrit Dhammapada (1921) — Noted the Chinese Fa-kheu-king chapter 38 as an Indian recension parallel of the Mahāmaṅgala-Jātaka.
